findings.quote: Gross margin has widened from 28.5% in FY22 to 31.0% in FY26
findings.issue: The gross-margin widening (28.5% FY22 to 31.0% FY26) is reintroduced with the numbers restated in four sections: thesis, financials.incomeCommentary ("gross margin widened from 28.5% to 31.0%"), businessMoat.moatFactors[Value gap] ("a widening gross margin, from 28.5% in FY22 to 31.0% in FY26") and growth.points ("gross margin has risen to 31.0% in FY26 from 28.5% in FY22"). The same restate-the-figure pattern affects three more clusters: the raised 7,500-store target with the +300/+200 split (analystCommentary, thesis, catalysts, businessMoat.segments, growth.points, capitalAllocation, finalRecommendation); the FY26 capital-returns figures ($4.3B returned, $1.3B in Q2, $2.5B repurchases, $1.8B dividends) across thesis, cashflowCommentary, capitalAllocation and finalRecommendation; and the consensus $169.80 / +29.0% across analystCommentary, catalysts, multiplesCommentary, scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation. Rubric 7 asks that each figure be introduced once and referred back to in words.
findings.fix: Introduce each figure once in its home section and refer back in words elsewhere (e.g. "the same gross-margin gain", "the raised store target", "the returns noted above", "the consensus target") instead of restating the numbers each time.
findings.note: Fixed across all four clusters. Gross margin now shows 28.5%/31.0% only in incomeCommentary; thesis, moatFactors[Value gap] and growth.points refer in words ("widened over recent years"). The 7,500/+300/+200 store target appears numerically only in growth.points; other sections say "raised store target". Returns: cashflowCommentary carries $2.5B/$1.8B, capitalAllocation carries $4.3B/$1.3B, thesis and finalRecommendation point in words ("FY26 shareholder returns noted above"). Consensus $169.80/+29.0% is numeric only in multiplesCommentary; elsewhere "the consensus target".

findings.quote: a target range of $150 to $180, above the current $131.59 and below the $169.80 consensus
findings.issue: The target high of $180 sits above the $169.80 consensus, so describing the $150 to $180 range as "below the $169.80 consensus" is internally inconsistent (rubric 6, calls coherence). Only the Base ($158) and the band midpoint ($165) are below consensus; the top is roughly 6% above it. scenarioCommentary carries the same loose framing: "the target range of $150 to $180 is set below the street to respect the non-recurring share of recent margin gains."
findings.fix: Attach the conservative framing to the base/midpoint, e.g. "our Base at $158 and the band midpoint sit below the $169.80 consensus, while the $180 top allows modest upside beyond it," so the stated band stays consistent with the consensus anchor.
findings.note: Resolved in both places. finalRecommendation.body[0] now reads "our Base at $158 and the low end of the range sit below the consensus target, while the $180 top allows modest upside beyond it"; scenarioCommentary now reads "Our Base and the low end of the range stay below consensus, while the $180 top of the range allows modest upside beyond it." The band is now consistent with the $169.80 consensus anchor.

findings.quote: a net-cash position that has deepened across the past five years
findings.issue: The net-debt series on the page does not deepen steadily: net cash was $2.9B in FY22 (net debt -2.9), fell to $2.1B in FY23 (-2.1), then -2.7 (FY24), -2.5 (FY25) and -3.4 (FY26). The endpoint is deeper than the start, but "deepened across the past five years" overstates the consistency of a series that wobbled in the middle years (rubric 2/9).
findings.fix: State that the balance sheet ended FY26 at its deepest net-cash position of the five years (-$3.4B), rather than implying a steady year-by-year deepening.
findings.note: Rewritten to "Net debt was -$3.4 billion in FY26, more net cash than the -$2.9 billion of FY22, though the balance did not build steadily — it narrowed to -$2.1 billion in FY23 before rebuilding to the FY26 level." The claim of a steady year-by-year deepening is gone.

findings.issue: The proxy states the related-party amounts were "consistent with other Associates at their levels and responsibilities." "Consistent with peers" in an executive-pay context can read as market or peer-company benchmarking rather than same-level colleagues; here the source's phrasing is the point (rubric 9).
findings.fix: Use the proxy's wording — "consistent with other Associates at their levels and responsibilities" — in place of "consistent with peers."
findings.note: Now uses the proxy's exact phrasing: "at compensation the proxy describes as consistent with other Associates at their levels and responsibilities."
